body:
**Independent — no blockers.**

### Problem

`src/app/template.tsx` is a root-level Next.js `template`, which is re-instantiated on every navigation. Everything below it remounts — including `DashboardShell` and `Sidebar`.

`src/components/dashboard/sidebar.tsx` holds `expandedMenus` as a plain `useState<Set<string>>(new Set())` with no persistence, so any submenu the user opens (Transactions, Invoices & Dues, Reports) collapses on the very next navigation. Its `useEffect` only re-expands the submenu containing the *active* route, so a submenu opened but not navigated into is always lost.

The settings sidebar already has this fixed — `src/hooks/use-settings-nav-state.ts` holds state in a module-level store synced to `sessionStorage` via `useSyncExternalStore`, precisely because component state does not survive the remount.

`src/hooks/use-sidebar-state.ts` (the icon-only width collapse) is **fine** — its `useState` lazy initializer re-reads `localStorage` on every mount. Do not change it.

### Change

New `src/hooks/use-sidebar-nav-state.ts` modelled on `use-settings-nav-state.ts`; replace `expandedMenus` with it, keeping the auto-expand-active behaviour as an overlay (`userToggled[id] ?? isActive`), matching `SettingsSidebar`.

### Verify

- Expand a submenu you are **not** currently inside, navigate elsewhere, confirm it is still expanded.
- `npm test`
